headlines.article_text: Disney (DIS) earnings Q4 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Disney topped Wall Street estimates for revenue and earnings per share for its fiscal fourth quarter. It's targeting $3 billion in cost savings by fiscal year 2029 via measures that include layoffs, CFO Hugh Johnston told CNBC. The company's results were once again boosted by strength in its streaming and parks divisions. In this article DIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 2:20 02:20 Disney tops estimates on revenue, EPS in fourth-quarter earnings Squawk Box Disney on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations and announced it's targeting $3 billion in cost savings by fiscal year 2029. Those cost-cutting efforts include several rounds of layoffs announced in recent months, Disney's Chief Financial Officer Hugh Johnston told CNBC. The most recent round, which seeks to reduce costs by up to 20%, was reported earlier this month . Future cost-saving measures will include reductions in administrative and other general expenses, Johnston said, while adding, "We do expect more layoffs." These cuts will help Disney fund its $26 billion in projected content spend for fiscal 2027, a 9% increase from fiscal 2026. The entertainment giant is also forecasting double-digit growth in earnings per share in the next fiscal year, as well as segment operating income growth of around 8%. Disney noted that the majority of that growth will be concentrated in the first half of the year due to the theatrical debut of "Avengers: Doomsday" and a boost from the Super Bowl, which will air on Disney's ESPN and ABC networks. "The growth is really going to come in the first half of this year," Johnston said. "That's the opposite of what we saw in '26, where the growth was backloaded." The company will also increase its annual dividend to $2 a share, a 33% increase from the previously declared dividend. It will be payable in two installments of $1 per share, one in January and one in July. Here's how Disney performed in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Oct. 3 , compared with what Wall Street expected, according to LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.77 adjusted vs. $1.67 expected Revenue : $25.95 billion vs. $25.18 billion expected Disney reported net income for the fiscal fourth quarter of $2.61 billion, or $1.51 per share, compared with $1.31 billion, or 73 cents per share, during the same period the year prior. Adjusting for one-time items, including severance and other restructuring charges as well as the value of intangible assets, Disney reported earnings per share of $1.77. The company's revenue for the quarter was 16% higher year over year, and results were once again lifted by its parks and streaming divisions. Strength in parks Disney's experiences segment, which includes its theme parks and cruises, reported nearly $10.11 billion in revenue, up 15% year over year. Operating income for the unit increased 20% to $2.25 billion. The division is already a top performer for the company, but it benefited in the fiscal fourth quarter because of an extra calendar week compared to the previous fiscal year. While international attendance continues to lag at Disney's domestic parks, it is being offset by domestic attendance, especially at the Walt Disney World resort in Orlando, Florida, Johnston said. Growth at Disneyland Paris was driven by recent investments including an expansion area called World of Frozen. Attendance at the Hong Kong and Shanghai parks remained soft because of broad economic challenges in those regions, according to Disney. The company expects operating income for the experiences segment to grow in the high-single digits in fiscal 2027. Growth is expected to be frontloaded as the company laps the launch of the Disney Adventure cruise ship, which set sail in March. Sports, streaming and entertainment Over at its entertainment division, Disney saw revenue increase 17% to $11.89 billion. Operating income nearly doubled to $1.33 billion. Revenue from streaming, specifically, rose 19% to $6.1 billion, Disney said. The segment benefited from the extra week on the fiscal calendar as well as from growth in subscription and affiliate fees. Additionally, the company saw higher theatrical distribution revenue from titles like "Toy Story 5." Disney said Tuesday it expects operating income for the entertainment division to grow in the high-single digits in the coming fiscal year. The company's sports division saw revenue increase 16% in the fiscal fourth quarter, reaching $4.61 billion. Operating income for the segment increased more than 50% to $1.39 billion. Subscription and affiliate fees fueled this growth alongside an increase in advertising revenue. The company expects its sports division's operating income to grow by double digits in fiscal 2027. It noted that the fiscal first quarter of the year will see some declines because of the timing of College Football Playoff games and the New Year's window. However, the fiscal second quarter will benefit from the college championship as well as the broadcast of Super Bowl 61. Disney's outlook for overall and segment results for fiscal year 2027 excludes the impact of a 53rd week in fiscal year 2026. Jordan Broggi has been chosen as CFO to replace McPhail. Decker, CEO since 2022, had been on temporary medical leave since August. The company said on Tuesday that Decker has returned from leave but is now stepping down from his role. He will continue to serve as chair of the board of directors, the company said. McPhail has been with the company since 2005, holding multiple executive roles. "We're not going to change course," McPhail told CNBC's Becky Quick. He said the company will continue to lean into winning professional shoppers like contractors and using AI tools to encourage sales. McPhail added that while the company faces more challenges now than it did at the start of the year, it is still winning share of the home improvement market. Home Depot has been pressured by a sluggish housing market, higher mortgage rates and a more cautious consumer. Still, the company has previously said it's seen resilience among its pro shoppers who are still shopping for their home improvement projects. In the third quarter, the company said online comparable sales grew around 13%, which marked its sixth straight quarter of double-digit positive growth for the metric. For the full year, Home Depot said it expects total sales to rise roughly 4.5%, the top end of its previously provided range. It also anticipates comparable sales will grow around 1.4%, compared with an outlook of flat to a 2% increase.
